componentsIndex.title: Components
componentsIndex.text: The component library of an IDE-styled portfolio. Pick a component to see a live demo — the whole interface is built from these blocks only.

props.title: Props
props.description: Name, type, default value and description of each prop. The list is read straight from the component's types file.

props.extends: Also accepts all props of type

tokens.none: This component does not use any @theme tokens — its behaviour comes from the layout (widths, margins).
tokens.footnote: The list is computed from the component's sources. Individual values measured on the prototype that are not tokens (e.g. custom shades) are not listed here.

overview.title: IDE-styled portfolio components
overview.text: OrchIDE UI is the component library the whole portfolio is built from, including this page. One palette, one type scale, and components checked against the prototype.

colors.title: Colours only from the theme
colors.body: The default is a dark IDE-style theme with an orchid accent. Code refers to tokens by name, so another theme is a new file, not changes in components.

tokens.title: Tokens instead of pixels
tokens.body: Text takes FontSize, TextColor and FontFamily instead of px values. Values outside the scale go to className.

fidelity.title: Fidelity to the prototype
fidelity.body: Styles are measured on the live prototype (computed style), not copied from a description. Each component records what it was verified against.

themes.title: Every colour comes from the theme.
themes.text: A theme is a set of colour tokens in a single file. Components, pages and the docs refer to them by name ({{count}} groups: surfaces, lines, content, accent, links, tones, decoration), so a new theme needs no code changes. There are two: dark (default) and light — the switch is in the header of this page and in the app's status bar.

groups.overlays: Translucent overlays: tint (hover wash), highlight (light edge), scrim (shadows)

steps.copy: Copy design-system/theme/light.css to theme/<name>.css, change <name> in the :root[data-theme='<name>'] selector and the values — keep the names. Shadows are optional.
steps.register: Add the name to ThemeName (design-system/theme/theme.ts) and import the file in src/index.css.
steps.check: Run npm run check:theme: the script checks that the theme has exactly the same tokens as the default one.
steps.use: A theme is chosen through useTheme() (or setTheme) — the choice is remembered, and a script in index.html applies it before the first render. The switch is a StatusBarSwitch with icon options.

items.raw: Raw colour values (hex notation, rgb and hsl functions) and default Tailwind palette classes are forbidden in code — ESLint enforces it; the palette itself is disabled.
items.alpha: A colour with transparency is a token with a modifier, e.g. bg-accent/10. Shadows are built from the scrim and tint tokens, so a theme defines only those two.
items.read: Places that cannot use a CSS variable (SVG as a data URI, canvas) read the value through readThemeColor().
items.attribute: data-theme must be set on <html>: derived tokens resolve on that element.

architecturediagram.summary: Vertical diagram of system layers with arrows, links to the code and rows of modules.
architecturediagram.note: The architecture card on the project page (Portfolio.cs) — the component draws the arrows; a connection's description is the block's `connectionLabel`.

badge.summary: A small status or date label, in a neutral or an accent tone.

chip.summary: A static technology tag with an optional icon, in five size variants.
chip.note: Icons are Lucide for now, eventually Devicon/Simple Icons in brand colours.

list.summary: A list with a header, a counter and an optional search field; rows with an animated hover.
list.note: ListItem row: on hover/activation an accent bar appears, the background lightens and the left padding grows.

gallery.summary: A carousel of project photos with placeholders, arrows, dots and keyboard support.
gallery.note: .project-gallery (Portfolio.cs / the project card) — checked in computed style.

card.summary: A bordered card with a header: a bar with a title and an action (Compact) or a light title (Standard); inside — lists, label/value fields or any content.
card.note: Replaced DataCard, InfoCard and CardHeading. Compact: .home-card, .home-techbar, .arch2 and “Company details” on Contact; Standard: Gallery and the project architecture card; Hero: the About the project card.

input.summary: A single-line text field with a label.

textarea.summary: A multi-line text field with a label and adjustable height.

searchfield.summary: A search field with an icon and a border.
searchfield.note: .solution-search (Solution Explorer). The Stack search is a private part of List.

text.summary: Text from tokens: size, colour, font and weight instead of px values.
text.note: An omitted parameter is inherited from the parent. Details outside the scale (letter-spacing, line-height) go in className.

label.summary: A small, uppercase heading: a kicker above a title or a panel bar.
label.note: A kicker above a heading (a panel heading with a counter — see List).

loader.summary: An IDE-style loading state: a thin progress bar and a status line with a blinking cursor.
loader.note: The moving bar respects the system reduced-motion setting. The error state shows the message without the bar.

button.summary: An action button (or a link that looks like one) in the Primary, Outline and Secondary variants and the Md, Sm, Xs and Lg sizes.

toolbarbutton.summary: An icon-only button in two sizes (Md and compact Sm) — bar tools (Terminal, Explorer).

iconbutton.summary: An icon-only button with a border — controls inside a card (e.g. the Gallery carousel arrows).

railbutton.summary: A navigation button with a vertical label, familiar from the IDE's left-hand rail.
railbutton.note: .rail button[data-go]/[data-skills] — active and hover states checked in computed style.

link.summary: An accent-coloured text link: a link (<a>) or an action button inside content.
link.note: .tour-action, .ai-message button, .explorer-contact-panel button — colours unified into a single link token.

container.summary: A centred page-width container with side margins.

panel.summary: The base card: background, border, radius and shadow. Optionally with a hover.

splitpanel.summary: Master-detail: a list on the left, details on the right; it collapses on narrow screens.
splitpanel.note: .xp in Experience and .stack-panel in Stack have an identical 320px/1fr grid, border and radius — checked in the DOM.

statusbar.summary: The bottom bar of the IDE window: branch, file path, panel toggles, language and version.
statusbar.note: .status in the prototype — dimensions and colours measured with getComputedStyle.

titlebar.summary: The top bar of the IDE window: logo, title and action buttons.
titlebar.note: .bar and .bar .run in the prototype — dimensions, colours and hover measured with getComputedStyle.

menu.summary: A table-of-contents card with flat items and expandable groups.

tabs.summary: Tabs of open files with closing and dragging to change the order.
tabs.note: .tabs — default/hover/active/close/dragging states measured in computed style, dragging built on pointer events.

solutionexplorer.summary: A file tree with a search field, collapsible folders and a collapsible panel.
solutionexplorer.note: .explorer/.solution-tree — indents, file markers and the active state, checked in computed style.

guide.summary: A step-by-step guide: a card, a spotlight on an element and a dimmed backdrop.
guide.note: .portfolio-tour-card/-shade/-highlight (the “Guide me” tour) — card, backdrop and highlight; the targets and steps are supplied by the app.

terminal.summary: A bottom console panel with command history, Tab completion and resizable height.
terminal.note: .portfolio-terminal — Esc closes it, the height changes by dragging or with arrows on the handle. Commands are interpreted by the app.

chat.summary: The assistant window with message bubbles, question chips and a message field.
chat.note: .ai-chat — Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a new line, Esc closes. Answers are generated by the app.

chatlauncher.summary: A floating “Ask about me” button that opens the chat window.
chatlauncher.note: .ai-chat-toggle — fixed position in the bottom-right corner; the bottom offset is animated (180 ms). Dimensions and colours measured in the prototype.
